children: The South African rand weakened on Thursday as a stronger dollar and higher oil prices weighed on the currency, while investors assessed a slew of domestic economic data that painted a mixed picture of Africa's most industrialised economy.
At 1300 GMT, the rand traded at 16.1750 against the dollar
, about 0.8% weaker than its previous close.

edged higher against a basket of currencies, while oil prices rose around 4% with benchmark Brent crude hitting $105 a barrel after the biggest spike in attacks on shipping since the start of the Iran war spurred trader concerns over supply disruptions.
Like other risk-sensitive currencies, the rand has been driven by global market sentiment, particularly since the start of the U.S.-Iran war on February 28, alongside domestic economic developments.
Data from Statistics South Africa showed mining output fell 7.5% year on year in July, while manufacturing output rose 1.1%.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected mining output to fall 2.8% and manufacturing output to slip 1.6%.

Separately, South Africa's central bank said the country recorded a current account deficit in the second quarter following a strong surplus in the first three months of this year, as the Iran war drove import costs sharply higher.

South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) also weakened, as the yield rose 3 basis points to 8.705%.
